before.title: Curves, regular causal curves and future timelike worldlines in affine Minkowski space
before.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space (def-sr-affine-minkowski-model) and let I be an order-convex subset of R with at least two elements (def-interval); a curve of the model is a map x: I -> A. (a) Derivative and regularity of the parametrization. For s in I and h nonzero with s + h in I the difference quotient (x(s+h) - x(s))/h is an element of V, the displacement from x(s) to x(s+h) divided by the real number h; the curve is differentiable at s when the limit of these quotients as h -> 0 exists in the finite-dimensional real vector space V, and then this limit, written x'(s) in V, is the tangent vector of x at s. If x_A: A -> R^4 is the chart of an inertial frame (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart), then x is differentiable at s exactly when the R^4-valued map x_A o x is differentiable at s in the sense of def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral, and then x'(s) = E((x_A o x)'(s)), where E: R^4 -> V is the frame isomorphism; this does not depend on the inertial chart used, because inertial chart transitions are affine, hence smooth (lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas), and all norms on the finite-dimensional V give the same limit. The curve is C^1 when it is differentiable at every point of I and the derivative map s |-> x'(s), I -> V, is continuous (def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity); it is C^k for k >= 1 when x' is C^{k-1}. A curve on a compact interval [a,b] contained in I is piecewise C^1 when there is a finite partition a = s_0 < s_1 < ... < s_m = b such that x is C^1 on every open subinterval (s_{i-1},s_i) and the one-sided derivatives at the s_i exist; derivatives at the endpoints of I are the one-sided limits over I. (b) Causal character. Let x be differentiable at s in I. Then x is regular at s if x'(s) is not the zero vector; x is timelike (respectively null, spacelike, causal) at s if the vector x'(s) is timelike (respectively null, spacelike, causal) in the sense of def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, and x is future-directed at s if x'(s) is future timelike or future null in the sense of def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets. The zero vector has no causal character, so only a regular curve has a causal character at s. (c) Worldlines. A future timelike worldline (massive worldline) is a C^1 curve x: I -> A with x'(s) future timelike for every s in I; a future causal curve (respectively a future null curve) is a C^1 curve with x'(s) future causal (respectively future null) for every s in I. A piecewise C^1 worldline is a piecewise C^1 curve all of whose one-sided tangents are future timelike, and a C^k worldline is a worldline whose parametrization is C^k; C^2 regularity is what makes the four-acceleration of this page available. The parametrization is part of the curve: the image of a future timelike worldline is also the image of the past-directed curve s |-> x(-s), which is not a worldline of this model, and no worldline or clock claim is attached to it. The definition asserts the existence of no worldline beyond those given by an explicit formula.
before.strategy: A definition item: it fixes the curve, regularity and causal-character language on which the page's items rest, and makes no proof claim beyond well-definedness. Obligations: (i) the difference quotient is an element of V because the affine action gives a displacement for every ordered pair of events, and the limit is taken in the finite-dimensional real vector space V, so no norm has to be chosen; (ii) the identification with the coordinate calculus and the independence of x'(s) and of C^k from the inertial chart are justified by the affine, hence smooth, chart transitions of lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas, with the published vector-valued derivative of def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral as the coordinate calculus; (iii) continuity of x' is continuity of a V-valued map (def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity), and one-sided derivatives at endpoints are limits over the domain I as in def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral; (iv) causal character and the future/past alternative are those of the model's vector classification and time orientation, with the zero vector excluded, so regularity is implicit in every causal character; (v) null and spacelike curves are distinguished from massive worldlines and are used later only to delimit the proper-time construction. No choice principle is used: all objects are finite-dimensional or explicitly parametrized.

after.title: Improper integrability and endpoint increments of weak piecewise future causal curves
after.statement: Let x:[a,b]->A, a<b, be a piecewise C^1 curve in the sense of def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline, with a finite partition a=s_0<...<s_m=b, C^1 on each open piece and finite one-sided difference-quotient derivatives at both ends of each piece. Assume its tangents are nonzero future causal at every open-piece point and at each one-sided endpoint. In any inertial chart write y=(y^0,z), z in R^3. On a piece (alpha,beta), choose r in (alpha,beta); for a function g continuous there, write integral_(alpha,beta) g for lim_(u downarrow alpha) integral_u^r g + lim_(v uparrow beta) integral_r^v g when both limits are finite. Then: (a) y is continuous on [alpha,beta], y^{0'}>=|z'|>=0 on (alpha,beta), and y^{0'}>0 there. (b) Every coordinate derivative is absolutely improperly Riemann integrable; its signed improper integral equals the corresponding endpoint increment. The continuous functions |z'| and f=sqrt((y^{0'})^2-|z'|^2)=sqrt(-eta(x',x')) have finite nonnegative improper integrals, with integral f<=integral y^{0'}=y^0(beta)-y^0(alpha). (c) The improper values are independent of r, additive under subdivision, and the finite piece sums are independent of the admissible partition. (d) D=x(b)-x(a) is nonzero future causal: D^0>0 and |D_spatial|<=D^0 in every inertial chart. If some interior or one-sided endpoint tangent is future timelike, D is future timelike. Coordinate time is strictly increasing on every nondegenerate subinterval. The integrals need not be ordinary closed-piece Riemann integrals. No derivative-limit hypothesis, Lebesgue-integration premise, clock identification, or choice principle is used.
after.strategy: Complete local adaptation of the flat future-cone integral argument, with endpoint integrability supplied rather than assumed. (a) Finite quotient derivative v at an endpoint gives x(t+h)-x(t)=h(v+o(1)), hence endpoint continuity; C1 gives interior continuity. The future cone coordinate criterion gives y0'>=|z'| and y0'>0 on each open piece. The square root is continuous on nonnegative reals: positive arguments use thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives with exponent 1/2; at zero, 0<=t<epsilon^2 implies 0<=sqrt(t)<epsilon. Thus the spatial norm and causal density are continuous even at a null tangent or a zero spatial component. Since y0'>=|z'|>=0, their squared values lie between 0 and (y0')^2, giving 0<=f<=y0' by the nonnegative square-root order. (b) On every alpha<u<v<beta, the derivative is continuous on [u,v], so thm-continuous-implies-integrable and thm-ftc-second-part give integral_u^v yj'=yj(v)-yj(u). Fix r inside. For y0' the left and right limits are y0(r)-y0(alpha) and y0(beta)-y0(r), finite by endpoint continuity and nonnegative. For any continuous 0<=g<=y0', the left truncation integrals are increasing as u decreases, bounded above by y0(r)-y0(alpha); completeness supplies their supremum S. Given epsilon>0 choose u* with integral_u*^r g>S-epsilon; every alpha<u<u* then has integral_u^r g between S-epsilon and S, proving the limit S. The right side is identical. Apply this to |yj'|, |z'| and f; all are continuous inside and bounded above by y0'. Signed coordinate integrals converge by the truncated FTC and endpoint continuity; thus each derivative is absolutely improperly integrable and has the exact endpoint increment. (c) Ordinary integral additivity on truncations and finite limits show independence of r and additivity under each interior cut. Any two admissible finite partitions have a common refinement, so all finite sums agree. (d) On truncations, the vector-integral norm inequality gives |z(v)-z(u)|<=integral_u^v |z'|<=integral_u^v y0'. Pass to endpoints and sum with the Euclidean triangle inequality to obtain |D_spatial|<=D0. Positive y0' on a compact interior interval gives a positive time increment, and nonnegativity on the rest gives D0>0; apply the same argument to any nondegenerate restriction for strict time monotonicity. At an interior timelike tangent, y0'-|z'| is continuous and positive in a compact interior neighborhood, so its integral is positive and the inequality becomes strict. At a left endpoint with timelike one-sided quotient v, (y(alpha+h)-y(alpha))/h tends to v, so for some h>0 that quotient is future timelike by openness of the cone. This subdisplacement is future timelike, and the remaining subdisplacement is future causal by the already proved non-strict inequality; adding their coordinates yields a future timelike sum. At a right endpoint use (y(beta)-y(beta-h))/h similarly. At a corner use the corresponding adjacent piece. This proves the endpoint-only timelike clause without continuity of the derivative at the corner. No closed-piece derivative integrability or countable choice is assumed.

before.title: Total proper time of a piecewise C^1 future timelike worldline
before.statement: Let c > 0 be the conversion constant of def-sr-proper-time and let x: [a,b] -> A be a future timelike worldline with a < b that is piecewise C^1 with partition a = s_0 < s_1 < ... < s_m = b (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline). Corner hypothesis (H): for every i = 1,...,m the derivative s |-> x'(s) of the open piece (s_{i-1},s_i) has finite one-sided limits at s_{i-1} and s_i in V; assigning those limits as endpoint values turns x' into a continuous V-valued map x'_i on the closed piece [s_{i-1},s_i]. Assume (H). Then: (i) for every i the real function g_i(t) := sqrt(-eta(x'_i(t), x'_i(t))) is continuous and strictly positive on [s_{i-1},s_i], hence Riemann integrable there (thm-continuous-implies-integrable); (ii) the total proper time of x from a to b is Delta tau(x) := c^{-1} sum_{i=1}^{m} integral_{s_{i-1}}^{s_i} g_i(t) dt; (iii) the value does not depend on the partition: every refinement of a partition satisfying (H) again satisfies (H) and gives the same sum by additivity of the integral over subintervals, and for any two partitions satisfying (H) the common refinement is a refinement of both, so the sums agree; (iv) if x is C^1 on [a,b] then (H) holds with the single piece [a,b] and Delta tau(x) = tau(b) - tau(a), the proper-time difference of def-sr-proper-time, so the two definitions agree; (v) Delta tau(x) > 0; for a piecewise inertial worldline (def-sr-inertial-and-piecewise-inertial-worldline) Delta tau(x) is the sum over the pieces of the straight-segment proper times c^{-1}(s_i - s_{i-1}) sqrt(-eta(d_i,d_i)); (vi) additivity over concatenation: if additionally a < b < d and x is a future timelike worldline on [a,d] that is piecewise C^1 with a partition having b as a partition point and satisfies (H) for that partition, then for the two restrictions x_1 := x restricted to [a,b] and x_2 := x restricted to [b,d] (each satisfying (H) for the induced partition) one has Delta tau_{[a,d]}(x) = Delta tau_{[a,b]}(x_1) + Delta tau_{[b,d]}(x_2). The item defines the integral only; the reading of an ideal clock along such a history is the separate clock hypothesis of post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and post-sr-free-trajectories-and-clock-hypothesis.
before.strategy: A definition item with well-definedness obligations. (i) Continuity of g_i: x'_i is continuous and V-valued, eta is bilinear and nondegenerate (def-lorentz-form-and-inertia), so in an eta-orthonormal basis (lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis) t |-> eta(x'_i(t),x'_i(t)) is a finite sum of products of continuous real functions (thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions); the square root is continuous on the positive reals (thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives, def-rational-power, thm-composition-of-continuous-functions). Strict positivity is the future timelike hypothesis on the tangents of the piece (including the one-sided values, which are future timelike because a piecewise C^1 worldline of def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline has future timelike one-sided tangents). Integrability is thm-continuous-implies-integrable for real-valued functions on a compact interval; the oriented convention is that of def-oriented-integral. (ii)-(iii) Partition independence: a refinement of an (H)-partition inherits (H), and thm-additivity-over-subintervals splits each piece integral; the common-refinement argument is then immediate. (iv) With m = 1 and x C^1 on [a,b], (H) holds because a C^1 derivative is continuous on [a,b] with its one-sided endpoint values; the integral is that of def-sr-proper-time. (v) For a piecewise inertial worldline the extended derivative on a piece is the constant d_i, so each piece integral is (s_i - s_{i-1}) times c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(d_i,d_i)), the straight-segment value of def-sr-proper-time. (vi) Concatenation: the induced partitions make the sum over the pieces of x the sum of the two sums. No choice principle is used; all integrals are Riemann integrals of continuous functions on compact intervals.

after.title: Total proper time of a piecewise C^1 future timelike worldline
after.statement: Let c>0 be the conversion constant of def-sr-proper-time and let x:[a,b]->A, a<b, be a piecewise C^1 future timelike worldline in the weak sense of def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline: x is C^1 on each open piece of a finite partition a=s_0<...<s_m=b, its interior tangents and finite one-sided difference-quotient endpoint tangents are future timelike, and continuous extension of the derivative is not assumed. (i) On each open piece let g_i(t)=sqrt(-eta(x'(t),x'(t)))>0. Define its two-ended improper Riemann integral by the convention of lem-sr-weak-piecewise-causal-integrability. That lemma proves each value finite and nonnegative; it is positive since g_i is positive and continuous on a compact interior subinterval. (ii) Define total proper time by Delta tau_[a,b](x)=c^{-1} sum_i integral_(s_(i-1),s_i) g_i. The finite sum is independent of the partition, by subdivision additivity and a common refinement. It is independent of the inertial chart because eta and the tangent are chart independent; constant Lorentz changes preserve the density already on each proper truncation. (iii) Define the based proper-time function tau_x(s)=Delta tau_[s0,s](x) for s>=s0, and tau_x(s)=-Delta tau_[s,s0](x) for s<s0, with tau_x(s0)=0, using restrictions and oriented limits. It is strictly increasing, and changing s0 changes only an additive constant. (iv) Corner hypothesis (H) is the special case in which each open-piece derivative has finite limits at both ends and thus extends continuously to the closed piece. Those limits equal the one-sided quotient derivatives. Under (H), each g_i extends continuously and positively to the closed piece, its improper integral equals its ordinary Riemann integral there, and the same finite-sum formula applies. In particular if x is globally C^1 on [a,b], Delta tau(x)=tau(b)-tau(a) of def-sr-proper-time. (v) Delta tau(x)>0. If on piece i the tangent is a constant future timelike vector d_i, the contribution is c^{-1}(s_i-s_(i-1))sqrt(-eta(d_i,d_i)); this gives the finite sum of straight-segment proper times. (vi) Additivity over concatenation: for a<b<d, restrictions of a weak piecewise worldline x on [a,d] satisfy Delta tau_[a,d](x)=Delta tau_[a,b](x)+Delta tau_[b,d](x). Insert b in the partition and use (ii). The definition supplies metric time only; identification with an ideal clock reading is the separate physical clock postulate. No global C^1 inverse, tangent at a kink, or four-acceleration at a kink is asserted.
after.strategy: Well-definedness is lem-sr-weak-piecewise-causal-integrability: endpoint continuity, finite improper integrals dominated in an inertial chart by the nonnegative time derivative, truncated FTC and partition independence. Strict positivity follows by a compact interior neighborhood on which g_i is positive and continuous. Refinements split each integral, and a common refinement gives independence of the finite partition. Restriction/additivity also give the based function, strict increase and base-point constants. Under (H), if the extended derivative is f_i, truncated FTC gives x(v)-x(u)=integral_u^v f_i. Passing u to the endpoint shows that the one-sided difference quotient is the average of f_i over a shrinking interval and therefore tends to its continuous endpoint value; thus the extension equals the finite quotient tangent. The extended density is continuous and strictly positive on the compact closed piece. Its bounded omitted endpoint tails tend to zero, so its improper value equals the ordinary Riemann value. Global C1 is the one-piece (H) case and agrees with def-sr-proper-time. Constant tangents give the displayed straight-segment calculation directly. All steps are finite-dimensional one-variable real analysis and use no choice principle; no physical premise supplies mathematical integrability.

after.title: Proper time is invariant under regular increasing weak piecewise changes of parameter
after.statement: Let c>0 and let x:[a,b]->A be a weak piecewise C^1 future timelike worldline. Let phi:[u,v]->[a,b] be an increasing continuous surjection, C^1 on the open pieces of a finite partition, with phi'>0 at every interior smooth point and finite positive one-sided difference-quotient derivatives at both endpoints of each piece. Then phi is strictly increasing with continuous inverse, y=x composed with phi is a weak piecewise C^1 future timelike worldline, and Delta tau_[u,v](y)=Delta tau_[a,b](x). The same equality holds for every pair of corresponding restricted parameter intervals; based proper-time functions differ only by their base-point constant. The relevant partition is the common refinement of phi's partition and the inverse images of x's partition points. This statement gives worldline/clock consequences only for positive derivatives, including all one-sided endpoint derivatives. It leaves intact the separate global-C^1 curve-integral identities allowing zero tangents in lem-sr-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance; a zero-tangent composition is not asserted to be a worldline.
after.strategy: On each closed piece phi is continuous and differentiable inside with phi'>0, so the mean value theorem proves strict increase there; finite concatenation gives global strict increase, and the continuous monotone bijection has continuous inverse. The finite inverse-image refinement separates all x and phi corners. Inside each refined piece componentwise chain rule gives y'=phi' x'(phi), so y' is continuous and future timelike and sqrt(-eta(y',y'))=phi' f(phi), where f=sqrt(-eta(x',x')). At each one-sided endpoint the quotient of y is the product of the corresponding quotient of x and that of phi; strict monotonicity chooses the correct side and both finite limits exist, the latter positive. Thus y has finite future timelike one-sided tangents and lies in the same weak class. On any compact interior truncation [r,s] of a refined piece, f is continuous on the compact image interval and phi' is continuous and integrable on [r,s]; thm-substitution gives integral_r^s phi' f(phi)=integral_phi(r)^phi(s) f. As r and s approach the refined endpoints, continuity and strict monotonicity of phi make the image endpoints approach the corresponding x endpoints. Both improper limits exist by lem-sr-weak-piecewise-causal-integrability for x and y, so the identity passes to the limits. Finite summation and partition independence give the full and restricted interval identities. Oriented additivity gives the based-function constant. before.title: Future cone, flat domain of dependence, absence of causal loops, time monotonicity and the straight-worldline proper-time maximum
before.statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space with the reachability objects <=, <, J^+, I^+ and R^+ of def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space. (a) Displacement of a future causal path. Let a < b be real numbers and let x: [a,b] -> A be a piecewise C^1 future causal path with D := x(b) - x(a). Then D is in Cbar^+. If x has a future timelike one-sided tangent at some point of [a,b], then D is in C^+. If x is nonconstant, then D is not 0. (b) Reachability and straight segments. J^+(p) = R^+(p), and for q not p one has q in J^+(p) if and only if the straight path s |-> p + s(q - p), s in [0,1], is a future causal path; moreover I^+(p) = {q : the straight path from p to q is future timelike} = {q : q is reachable from p by a piecewise C^1 future causal path having a future timelike one-sided tangent at some point}, and p is in neither of these two sets. (c) No causal loops. If p <= q and q <= p then p = q; equivalently there is no nonconstant piecewise C^1 future causal path x: [a,b] -> A with x(b) = x(a). (d) Time monotonicity. For the chart x of every inertial frame and every piecewise C^1 future causal path y: [a,b] -> A, the composition x^0 o y is nondecreasing, and if y is nonconstant on a subinterval [a',b'] of [a,b] then (x^0 o y)(b') > (x^0 o y)(a'); in particular every inertial frame agrees that a nonconstant future causal path does not go backwards in coordinate time. (e) Straight-worldline maximum. Let p,q be events with q in I^+(p), put D := q - p and T := sqrt(-eta(D,D)) > 0. Then for every piecewise C^1 future timelike worldline y: [a,b] -> A with y(a) = p and y(b) = q, the elapsed proper time c^{-1} sum_i (tau_i(b_i) - tau_i(a_i)), computed piecewise with the proper-time function tau_i of def-sr-proper-time on the C^1 pieces a = a_1 < b_1 = a_2 < ... < b_m = b, is at most T/c; equality holds if and only if the image of y is the straight segment from p to q and y traverses it with a strictly increasing time coordinate, i.e. y is a strictly increasing reparametrization of s |-> p + sD. (f) Invariance. For every proper orthochronous affine Lorentz map F of the model one has F(J^+(p)) = J^+(F(p)) and F(I^+(p)) = I^+(F(p)) for every event p, and p <= q if and only if F(p) <= F(q) for all events p,q. (g) Scope. The theorem concerns the affine model: it attaches no physical interpretation to <=, J^+, I^+ and R^+, asserts nothing about partial differential equations, propagation of particular fields or differentiability beyond piecewise C^1, and uses no choice principle.

(f) If F(p) = F(p_0) + L(p - p_0) with L proper orthochronous (def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group), then F(p + Cbar^+) = F(p) + L(Cbar^+) = F(p) + Cbar^+ because L preserves the future and past closed cones (thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra(iv)), which is exactly F(J^+(p)) = J^+(F(p)) and likewise for C^+ and I^+; the relation form follows. before.statement: Let c > 0 and let x: [a,b] -> A be a future timelike worldline with a < b that is piecewise C^1 with partition a = s_0 < s_1 < ... < s_m = b and satisfies the corner hypothesis (H) of def-sr-piecewise-proper-time. before.title: The endpoint bound for proper time and the maximality of the straight worldline in affine Minkowski space
before.statement: Let c > 0 and let x: [a,b] -> A be a future timelike worldline with a < b that is piecewise C^1 with partition a = s_0 < s_1 < ... < s_m = b and satisfies the corner hypothesis (H) of def-sr-piecewise-proper-time, with total proper time Delta tau(x) of def-sr-piecewise-proper-time. Put p := x(a), q := x(b) and T := sqrt(-eta(q-p,q-p)), a positive real number (lem-sr-endpoint-displacement-of-a-future-timelike-worldline). Then: (i) Endpoint bound: c Delta tau(x) <= T. (ii) Equality case: c Delta tau(x) = T if and only if x is a strictly increasing reparametrization of the straight segment from p to q, that is: there is a continuous strictly increasing surjection sigma: [a,b] -> [0,1] with sigma(a) = 0 and sigma(b) = 1, C^1 on every open piece of a partition of [a,b] satisfying (H), with sigma'(s) > 0 at every point of each open piece and finite one-sided limits at the partition points, such that x(s) = p + sigma(s)(q - p) for every s in [a,b]; equivalently x'(s) is a positive multiple of q - p at every point at which x is differentiable. (iii) Strictness: if the image of x is not contained in the straight segment {p + lambda(q-p) : 0 <= lambda <= 1}, then c Delta tau(x) < T; in particular, if x is piecewise inertial and its piece tangents d_1,...,d_m are not all positive multiples of one another (equivalently, its image is not contained in the straight segment), then the inequality is strict, while a piecewise inertial itinerary whose piece tangents are all positive multiples of one another has the straight segment as image and attains the bound. (iv) Straight worldlines attain the bound: for the inertial worldline x_s(s) := p + ((s-a)/(b-a))(q-p) one has c Delta tau(x_s) = T, in agreement with the straight-segment value of def-sr-proper-time; more generally every worldline whose image is the straight segment and which is traversed in the future direction attains the bound. (v) Scope: the theorem concerns the affine Minkowski model with a fixed positive constant c; it is a statement about the curve class (H) only, it does not identify proper time with any clock reading, and it asserts nothing about maximality of geodesics in curved spacetimes or in Lorentzian manifolds with different global structure.
before.strategy: Proof by reduction to the rest frame of the endpoint displacement. Write xi := x_A o x = (xi^0, xi_vec); as in lem-sr-endpoint-displacement-of-a-future-timelike-worldline, on each closed piece xi is continuous with continuously extendable derivative, and pointwise xi^{0'} > |xi_vec'| >= 0. Therefore the nonnegative continuous function h_i := xi^{0'} - sqrt((xi^{0'})^2 - |xi_vec'|^2) is defined and continuous on each closed piece, with h_i(s) >= 0 and h_i(s) = 0 exactly where xi_vec'(s) = 0. The total proper time is c Delta tau(x) = sum_i integral_{s_{i-1}}^{s_i} sqrt((xi^{0'})^2 - |xi_vec'|^2) dt <= sum_i integral_{s_{i-1}}^{s_i} xi^{0'} dt = xi^0(b) - xi^0(a) = T, where the last equality is the coordinate increment (per-piece primitive argument as in lem-sr-endpoint-displacement-of-a-future-timelike-worldline, using thm-ftc-first-part and cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant), and the inequality is thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral applied piecewise with additivity thm-additivity-over-subintervals. This proves (ii). (iii) is the contrapositive of (ii): if the image is not contained in the straight segment, x is not such a reparametrization, so equality fails, while (i) gives <=. (iv) is the computation x' = (q-p)/(b-a) with -eta = T^2/(b-a)^2 and integral over [a,b] equal to T, or clause (ii) with the affine sigma(s) = (s-a)/(b-a).
